slides.title: Standard Offering Release 26
slides.subtitle: Two step-by-step visuals: the Standard Offering inside Jaspersoft Server, and the database deployment of the snapshots and the objects the domains depend on  |  September 2026

slides.title: Standard Offering In Jaspersoft, Step By Step

steps.title: Author on Origin_DEV
lines: Every domain, Ad Hoc view, report and dashboard is built in the Workstreams tree on the internal server: the only place anything is edited by hand.

steps.title: Inventory and classify the export
lines: The org export is scanned for domains, Ad Hoc views, report units, dashboards and the datasource. Matching uses the business-facing labels, never the generic internal ids.

steps.title: Select the offering
lines: Only the Standard Offering list is kept, remapped into nine workstream folders by business process. The Workstreams tree is left untouched: a curated copy, not a move.

steps.title: Carry only what it needs
lines: One packaged copy of each domain (53 today) in one business-process home, every report and view reference rewritten to that copy, and the datasource resource carried because the domains reference it.

steps.title: Clean the package
lines: Print-wrapper reports stripped from saved Ad Hoc views, dashboards tied to public templates left out, folder metadata generated, the import index narrowed to the offering folder plus the datasource.

steps.title: Prove on Origin_TEST
lines: The first promotion, with the seven proofs: import without warnings, re-export byte-equal inside the scope, every resource executed, datasource connection unchanged.

steps.title: Client test org
lines: The datasource switched to the client's test database by carrying the target's own datasource export byte for byte; org path, folder, alias and tenant root rewritten; verified before import.

steps.title: Sweep and sign off
lines: Every view queried, every report rendered, every domain probed on the client's own numbers. PASS, EMPTY, SLOW or FAIL per resource with its timing; one sign-off document per org.

steps.title: Client prod org
lines: The same tool and the same proofs with an explicit prod flag. A repository inventory snapshot before and a diff after are the rollback record.

steps.title: Keep it current
lines: Additive-only domain patches with seven proofs and a one-command restore, the Standardized Reports folder for scheduled SQL reports, and every change swept and re-signed.

slides.legend: Steps 1 to 5 build the package once; steps 6 to 9 repeat per client org; step 10 is every change after go-live.

slides.title: Database Deployment, Step By Step

steps.title: Preflight
lines: Proves the deploy user can read every CISADM table the snapshots need and write the target objects. A limited-privilege variant exists for locked-down instances.

steps.title: Create the seven rolling snapshot tables
lines: Financial transactions, billed usage, SQ usage, GL distribution, measurements, usage and usage scalar detail: created empty with their keys, nothing loaded yet.

steps.title: Create the domain-support objects
lines: The SA aged-balance snapshot table, its snapshot-type lookup seed, and eight CMS views for device, asset, crew, field activity and case, with grants and the read-schema synonyms repaired.

steps.title: Deploy the procedures
lines: One baseline procedure per snapshot (the retained 24 months, loaded once) and one operational procedure; the aged-balance refresh procedure for the SA snapshot.

steps.title: Submit the baselines
lines: All eight loads submitted at once as database scheduler jobs; they run unattended and survive a dropped connection. The SA snapshot refresh runs alongside from live financial transactions.

steps.title: Ready gate
lines: The scheduler's job table is polled up to eight hours until every job reports SUCCEEDED. A FAILED or missing job stops the rollout.

steps.title: Validate and gate
lines: Row counts, twelve monthly totals against the source, duplicate keys. The install gate fails on any empty table or duplicate key. Domain support: views valid, lookup seeded, aging buckets sum to the balance, FT parity.

steps.title: Post-load indexes
lines: Indexes on the keys and dates the domains filter on, created after the load so the baseline is never slowed by them.

steps.title: Rolling cutover
lines: Rolling procedures installed (3 months rebuilt, 24 kept; 6-month at CityCorp and Odessa), one operational refresh run by hand and validated again. Long refreshes run as background jobs, never in the session.

steps.title: Schedule and monitor
lines: One scheduler job per table, twice daily with a 30-minute stagger, held on TEST until approved. Last-run capture and data-quality checks per client; validate again after the first scheduled run.

slides.legend: Steps 1 to 8 are the baseline; 9 and 10 are the cutover to rolling refresh. The domain-support objects ride the same rollout so the live domains work the day the snapshots do.

slides.title: The Objects The Domains Depend On (1 of 2)
rows: One end-of-day (LDAY) aged-balance row per service agreement: current and payoff balance, new charges, and ten aging buckets built from frozen ARS financial transactions dated up to today. Credits and payments retire the oldest debt first; excess credit sits in the current bucket; buckets 1 to 5 always sum to the current balance; future-dated amounts are excluded.
Debt Management: the SA Snapshot Aged Balance domain, its account roll-up (a derived query over this table, not a second object), and every aged-debt view and dashboard on it
The four snapshot-type codes (LDAY, EMON, ARCH, LEMN) written into the C2M lookup tables. The domain inner-joins them, so a fresh database without the seed returns zero rows in every Ad Hoc view.
Debt Management: SA Snapshot Aged Balance domain
One row per device with its identifiers pivoted from rows into columns: asset id, badge number, serial number, internal meter number, external and MDM ids, NIC id and serial, name, utility device id.
Meter Operations: Device domain; Daily Installations, Disconnected Service Points, Meters Not Recently Read
The device's business-object data area parsed out of its XML: business object code, latest status, retirement date and time. One row per device.
One row per asset with its identifiers pivoted into columns, the asset-side twin of the device identifier view, so the Asset domain can join by badge, serial or external id.
Meter Operations: Asset domain; In Storage, Distribution of Installed Assets, Non-Meter Assets

slides.title: The Objects The Domains Depend On (2 of 2)
rows: Field representative (crew member) mobile details parsed out of the representative's XML data area: the service areas they cover and their worker capabilities, one row per representative and area or capability.
Field Operations: Crew domain and its views
Activity characteristics pivoted per field activity: internal field-activity status, priority, and the third-party representative code, so the domain filters on them as columns.

The field activity's business-object data parsed from XML: instructions and comments, the appointment window and who took it, expiration, requester, external references, and the customer and contact names and phone numbers.
Field Operations: Crew and Field Activity domains; Upcoming Field Work, Cancelations, Average Days per Field Task

One row per case with its create and close timestamps derived from the case log (the case-created entry and the closing status entry) and the duration in minutes, measured to now while the case is open.
Customer Operations: Case domain and every case view
The case log as a timeline: every status change with the previous status, the previous log time, and how long the case sat in the previous and the current state.
Customer Operations: Case domain (state durations and the case timeline views)
slides.legend: All ten objects are created by one wrapper step in the rollout, validated by their own pack, and gated before the snapshots are scheduled; the CISREAD synonyms are repaired in the same step because CityCorp shipped with synonyms pointing at missing objects.
